expIntro.message: In “My models” every model has a button that opens its folder in Windows Explorer. Two small files are needed for that – the two steps below set them up. All of this is optional: leave it out and everything else keeps working unchanged, only that one button stays without effect.

expPathLabel.message: Full path to exactly this target folder

expPathHelp.message: It has to be the same folder you picked under “Target folder” – just as a full path. You can find it by opening the folder in Explorer and clicking the address bar at the top.

expNeedsPath.message: Enter the path of your target folder, otherwise the button stays hidden.

expPathMismatch.message: The path does not end with “$NAME$”. That is the folder you selected above – enter the same one here, otherwise the button opens the wrong directory.

expNoTargetYet.message: Select a target folder above first.

expOwnIntro.message: Two small files that we generate here. Both are shown below in plain text – so you can see exactly what ends up on your computer. That is the difference to a ready-made program, where you have to trust the vendor.

expOwnSafety.message: What the script can do: it checks whether the given folder exists and opens it in Explorer. Nothing else – it starts no other programs and deletes nothing. The registry file only writes under your own user account, not system-wide.

expOwnVbsNote.message: Note: the script uses VBScript because that runs without a window flashing up. Microsoft has deprecated VBScript – at some point it will disappear from Windows. Until then it works reliably; after that this feature would need a different approach.

expTestFailed.message: No response from the script. Either it is not set up yet, or the registry file was not run. The address called was: $URL$

libExpNoPath.message: The path of your target folder is still missing.

libExpNoScript.message: The script for opening Explorer is not set up. You can find the instructions in the settings.

expUndoText.message: This file removes the registry entry again. The script itself stays in place and can be deleted afterwards, along with its folder.

expAssignFailed.message: No response from the script. Either you closed the Windows dialog without picking a folder – or the script is not set up. In that case, go through steps 1 to 5 again.

expAssignDialogTitle.message:
Pick the same folder you granted under “Target folder” in the extension – the one your models are saved in.
Not your downloads folder, and not the folder of a single model.

expAssignDialogError.message:
That is not the folder the extension uses.

It means the folder you granted under “Target folder” – the one your downloaded models are in. Start again and pick that one.

expNeedsPermission.message: Linking needs write access to the target folder. Renew it above under “Target folder”, then try again here.

expScriptOld.message: The installed script is an older version ($ALT$ instead of $NEU$). Download it again in step 2 and replace the file in the folder – the registry file stays as it is.

expManualSummary.message: Enter the path by hand instead

stoppedNoneText.message: This page opened by itself because no target folder has been set yet – without one the extension cannot save anything. Pick a folder below, then start the download again.

stoppedPermText.message: This page opened by itself because Chrome no longer grants access to your target folder. Press “Renew permission” below and choose “Allow on every visit”. Then start the download again.

welcomeIntroUpdateFrom.message: The extension was updated from version $VON$. Here is what changed:

welcomeIntroInstall.message: This extension downloads models from MakerWorld, Printables and Thingiverse into sorted folders automatically. One click on “Download” on the site is enough – the files end up on your drive with proper names, ZIP archives already unpacked.

welcomeIntroUpdate.message: The extension has been updated. Here is what changed:

welcomeFooter.message: This page only appears once after an update. The full list of changes is in the changelog on GitHub.

welcomeSetupText.message: Choose where the files should be saved. Without a target folder the extension stops every download – that is the price for Chrome never asking about the location again.

welcomeF1Text.message: An overview of everything you downloaded – with preview images, search and a filter by platform. Each model shows the files it contains, and you can delete it from there too. Reachable from the extension’s icon.

welcomeF2Text.message: Downloads on these two platforms are now intercepted before the browser even starts them. Chrome no longer asks where to save – not even when a ZIP archive is unpacked. Thingiverse already worked this way.

welcomeF3Text.message: A small bar in the bottom right shows what is being downloaded and unpacked – and speaks up when something did not work.

welcomeF4Text.message: If you like, you can set up a button that opens a model’s folder straight in Windows Explorer. The settings page creates two small files for that and shows their contents in plain text. Entirely optional – everything else works without them.

welcomeF5Titel.message: The target folder is now required

welcomeF5Text.message: Files used to land in “Downloads/STL_Downloads” without any choice. That route went through Chrome’s download function – and therefore through the save-location dialog as soon as someone had “Ask where to save each file” enabled. A download is now stopped rather than taking that detour.

welcomeF2TextInstall.message: The extension intercepts the download before the browser starts it. Chrome therefore never asks where to save – not even when a ZIP archive is unpacked into many separate files.

welcomeFooterInstall.message: This page only appears once. All changes to the extension are listed in the changelog on GitHub.

vbsHeader.message:
Opens a folder in Windows Explorer and, when asked, reports its full
path back.
Windows runs this script when an address starting with stldl: is clicked.
Part of the Chrome extension "3D Model Auto-Downloader".

If something goes wrong it writes open-folder.log next to itself – that
file says what actually arrived. When all goes well, nothing is written.

vbsVersion.message:
Version of this script. It is the first line of every reply, so the
extension can recognise an outdated script.

vbsFiles.message: Names of the files the script and the extension talk through.

vbsUtf8.message:
Builds characters from a sequence of bytes. Needed because a character
such as an en dash takes three bytes in UTF-8 – without this step it
would become three characters instead of one, and the folder could not
be found.

vbsUrlDecode.message:
Resolve percent escapes: Chrome encodes the address before Windows
passes it on – a colon arrives as %3A, for example.

vbsReadFile.message: Reads a small text file. Returns an empty string if it does not exist.

vbsSetup.message:
--- Task: report our own path ------------------------------------------

The extension does not know the full path of its target folder – Chrome
never hands it out. So it drops a marker into the folder and calls this
task. We ask the user for the folder and only answer if the marker is
inside it. That proves it is the same folder – and no foreign path can
be obtained this way.

vbsFolderFlags.message: &H1 = real folders only, 17 = start at "This PC"

vbsUnicode.message: Unicode (third parameter True), otherwise accents in the path are lost

vbsScheme.message: Strip the "stldl:" scheme, and any leading slashes too

vbsTask.message:
A question mark means: a task, not a path. The fields are separated by |
because that character is not allowed in Windows paths.

vbsTrailingSlash.message: Remove a trailing backslash, otherwise FolderExists finds nothing

vbsSafety.message:
Safety net: only open folders that exist, never execute anything.
No program can be started through this address.

vbsHeartbeat.message:
Leave a sign of life in the opened folder. The extension looks for it a
moment later and knows from it that the script really ran – a protocol
call gives no feedback at all. The extension deletes the file right away.

regRegister.message:
Registers the "stldl:" scheme with Windows and links it to the script
open-folder.vbs. Part of the Chrome extension
"3D Model Auto-Downloader".

regUndoHint.message:
To undo this, the settings of the extension offer the file
stldl-protokoll-entfernen.reg.

regUndo.message:
Removes the "stldl:" scheme again. The minus sign in front of the key
name means delete. Affects this user account only, nothing system-wide.

The script open-folder.vbs stays where it is – you can simply delete it
afterwards, together with its folder.

expS6Dialog.message: The first time, Chrome asks one more thing first: “Open Microsoft ® Windows Based Script Host?” – that is the script being started, not the folder picker yet. Tick “Always allow …” there and confirm. With that box ticked the question stays away – without it, it comes back on every “Open in Explorer”.

libTrashEmptyConfirm.message: Permanently delete all $COUNT$ models in the trash? This cannot be undone.

libTrashNote.message: Deleted models stay in the folder _Trash_ inside your target folder until you empty the trash.

libDeleteForeverConfirm.message: Permanently delete “$NAME$”? The folder and every file in it will be removed from the disk – this cannot be undone.

modelPick.message: Pick a file on the left.

modelHelp.message: Drag = rotate · Right button = pan · Wheel = zoom

modelNoPreview.message: There is no preview for $TYPE$ files.

modelNoWebgl.message: This browser has no WebGL 2 – without it the model cannot be displayed. You can still open the files in Explorer.

modelReadFailed.message: “$FILE$” could not be read. The file may be damaged.

vbsAskText.message:
This script will copy itself into your user folder and then open stldl-protokoll.reg so Windows knows the “stldl:” scheme. Windows will ask again before that happens.

After that you pick your target folder.

Location:

vbsDoneText.message: Done. You can close this window and go back to the browser – it now says that everything is set up.

vbsDoneNoFolder.message: The script is set up, but no target folder was chosen. You can assign it later in the settings.

vbsRegMissing.message: The file stldl-protokoll.reg is not next to this script. Download both files again in the settings and keep them in the same folder.

vbsCopyFailed.message: The script could not copy itself into your user folder.

vbsInstall.message:
--- Setting up by double-click ------------------------------------

Called without parameters, the script sets itself up: it creates its
folder, copies itself into it and opens the registry file next to it.
It does not write the entry itself - Windows does that, with its own
confirmation, so the change stays visible.

vbsAskFirst.message:
Ask first, act second. A double-click must not do anything the user
did not expect.

vbsRegStep.message:
The registry file sits next to this script, where the browser put
them both. Open it visibly instead of importing it silently: Windows
is meant to ask.

vbsFolderStep.message:
Finally the target folder. The marker inside proves it is the
folder the extension is waiting for.

vbsMarker.message:
No marker in the folder, no answer - otherwise any path could be
obtained through this route.

expSetupS1Text.message: One click downloads two files into your downloads folder – open-folder.vbs and stldl-protokoll.reg – and opens it in Explorer. Keep them next to each other: the script looks for the second one beside itself. Older files of the same name are replaced so no copy with “(1)” in its name appears.

expSetupS2Text.message: Windows first asks whether you really want to run the file – it came from the internet, hence the question. Then the script explains what it does, Windows confirms the registry entry, and finally you pick your target folder – exactly the one you granted above under “Target folder” for your model files. Any other folder is rejected.

expSetupWaiting.message: Waiting for open-folder.vbs. Double-click the file in your downloads folder now – this page notices by itself once it has worked.

expSetupOk.message: Set up: $PATH$. The Explorer button in “My models” works now.

expSetupTimeout.message: No answer. Did you run the script? You can double-click it again at any time – or press the button above once more.

expSetupDownloaded.message: Downloaded. The folder should have opened – double-click open-folder.vbs there.

regPlain.message:
When you click "Open in Explorer", this entry runs exactly one command
line, namely this one:

regPlainHex.message:
The @=hex(2): line below holds exactly that command line - character by
character as hex, nothing else.

Plain text is not possible here. The .reg format writes plain text only
as an ordinary string (REG_SZ), and that type does not expand
%LOCALAPPDATA% - Windows would even mistake the %L inside it for one of
its own placeholders. The type needed is REG_EXPAND_SZ, and the file
format knows it only as hex(2).

To see in plain text what actually arrived, run afterwards:
  reg query "HKCU\Software\Classes\stldl\shell\open\command"

vbsTargetStore.message:
Remembers the assigned target folder next to the script. Every later
call is compared against it - see the check further down.

vbsGuard.message:
Safety gate: a registered URL scheme can be invoked by any website,
not just this extension. Only the assigned target folder and what
lies inside it are opened. The comparison is pure text work and
happens before the script touches the path: merely asking whether
a folder \\server\x exists would make Windows sign in there and
send the credentials along.
Paths containing .. are refused: they would pass the comparison and
still end up somewhere else.
